text:
incident-bot: paging: SLO alert - inference-p95 > 1.5s across us-west-2 (auto-threshold). Autoscale didn't spin up fast enough :rotating_light:

maya: I'm seeing a slow creep in the continuous prefetcher's KV cache size on gpu-pool-3, then queue length spikes and node flaps. A couple of pods restarted with CUDA OOMs.

simon: confirmed. logs show repeated: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory` from /srv/runtime/src/batcher/continuous_prefetcher.cc:421 and then container restart backoff.

eli: stack snippets: ```
[2026-03-15T20:10:12Z] prefetcher: kv_cache_size=1.9G, inflight_batches=128, queue_depth=10240
[2026-03-15T20:10:13Z] batcher: enqueue_time=450ms, dequeue_time=0ms, pending=10200
[2026-03-15T20:10:14Z] cuda: out of memory
```

lena: that enqueue/dequeue pattern looks like a growth spiral: prefetch keeps injecting new prefixes, continuous batching aggregates but never drains because GPU scheduling is blocked -> memory climbs -> OOM -> restart -> repeat.

maya: initial quick mitigation: can we disable continuous prefetch on the affected pool? That should stop new inflight prefixes and let things drain.

simon: I can patch the runtime config in k8s for gpu-pool-3: `runtime.CONTINUOUS_PREFETCHER.enabled: false` then rollout restart. Doing `kubectl -n redwood patch cm runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"CONTINUOUS_PREFETCHER.enabled":"false"}}'` and trigger rollout.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: triggered restart for deployment inference-runtime-gpu-pool-3 (3/5 pods restarted). Watch: https://k8s.console/cluster/pods/inference-runtime-gpu-pool-3

maya: queued downscales in the prefetcher too — set `PREFETCH_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8` in the config to stop ramp bursts. Simon, please patch that as well.

simon: patched PREFETCH_MAX_CONCURRENCY=8 and PREFETCH_RATE_LIMIT=200/s. Rolling restart continuing. Patch landed at 20:18 UTC.

eli: after the config changes, one pod still reported OOM on restart but the overall p95 started to drop. p95 went from ~1.9s -> 0.9s within 3 minutes.

cs-rep: CS note: we have two paying customers (acme-inc and maply) who reported 5xxs starting 20:07 UTC. I've opened customer tickets and informed them we're mitigating and will follow up.

maya: good. we should also set an emergency routing rule: route requests hitting >20s queue wait to a fallback smaller model (cpu fallback) to avoid cascades. Can infra set a temporary routing policy?

lena: I'll add a circuit-breaker route for the pool: `route.policy=soft-failover: fallback-model=distil-01`. Pushing now.

incident-bot: incident created INC-2026-0315-12 (severity: S2). Pager duty: oncall-eng, oncall-sre.

eli: action log summary so far: 1) disabled continuous prefetcher on gpu-pool-3 2) throttled PREFETCH_MAX_CONCURRENCY and PREFETCH_RATE_LIMIT 3) rolled restarts of affected pods 4) added soft-failover route to fallback model 5) CS notified customers.

maya: next steps: keep pool at reduced concurrency, monitor KV cache growth metric `prefetch.kv_bytes` and `batcher.pending_requests`. If stable for 30m, we can re-enable with stricter caps (max inflight 64, max prefix age 2s).

simon: note for root cause investigation: need heap/traces from one of the restarted pods before it fully recycles. If anyone can capture `gcore` or runtime heap dump, do it now. Also capture `nvidia-smi -q -x` and dmesg.

lena: I grabbed a heap snapshot and uploaded to /internal/incident/INC-2026-0315-12/artifacts (link withheld). Also grabbed `batcher` internal metrics showing a sustained 30s enqueue latency when the spiral began.

ops-bot: autoscaler: no new nodes launched for gpu-pool-3 because scale-out threshold evaluation was delayed by metric aggregation lag (investigating).

maya: note for postmortem: look at prefetcher heuristics that allowed unbounded growth under slow dequeue conditions. Also validate autoscaler metric latency and whether scale decisions should consider pending queue depth not just GPU utilization.

cs-rep: updating customers: "we mitigated the issue by throttling prefetch and activating a fallback model; some requests experienced errors while we recovered. We will follow up with root cause and timeline."

simon: handoff to next oncall in 2 hours. I'll leave runbook steps in the incident doc:
- check `prefetch.kv_bytes` < 800MB
- check `batcher.pending_requests` < 2000
- ensure `CONTINUOUS_PREFETCHER.enabled=false` for affected pools
- confirm fallback route active
- escalate to infra-sre if OOMs resume

maya: tagging infra-sre and runtime-team for RCA. Also assigning postmortem owner: @simon.

incident-bot: reminder: please set incident status to "mitigated" once p95 < 1s and customer-facing errors stop for 30m.

eli: metrics show p95 at 0.72s and 5xx rate near baseline at 20:47 UTC. I'm marking mitigated in the doc.

maya: handback: @oncall-next (simon covering until 23:00 UTC). Leave a note in pagerduty if things reoccur.

simon: acknowledged. I'll follow up with an initial RCA draft in the incident tracker and schedule a permanent fix: add backpressure in the prefetcher that falls back to token-limited sampling instead of unbounded prefix injection.

cs-rep: customers notified about mitigation and next steps. Will request credit for impacted windows.

lena: final: capture point-in-time snapshots for postmortem: heap, nv-smi logs, enqueue/dequeue metrics. Uploaded.

maya: thanks team. closing ephemeral channel and moving notes to /incidents/INC-2026-0315-12/postmortem. :white_check_mark:
